messages:
Alex: Quick heads-up — during the int8 canary for harbor-lite I saw duplicate tool invocations when streaming was enabled. Posting timeline and logs.

Sasha: ugh, duplicate how? same request id or different? :thinking_face:

Alex: Same client-side request id but two POSTs to /tools/annotate within 200ms. Looks tied to stream chunk that contains the function call trigger. Snippet below.

Jin: paste logs pls

Alex: ```
# stream chunks (server -> client)
chunk 1: {"type":"text","content":"...","partial":true}
chunk 2: {"type":"function_call","name":"annotate","args":"{\"text\": \"foo\"", "partial": true}
chunk 3: {"type":"text","content":"...","partial":true}
chunk 4: {"type":"function_call","name":"annotate","args":"{\"text\": \"foo\"}\n"}
# result: client parsed two separate function calls
```

Maria: Interesting — any difference vs fp16 run?

Alex: fp16 didn't duplicate. Quantization seems to change chunk boundaries. PTQ/decoder schedule appears to flush a func_call token twice in stream halves.

Sasha: canary-bot, did the canary run the streaming-holdback config or immediate-forward? @canary-bot

canary-bot: Canary run 5902468: model=harbor-lite-int8, stream_mode=chunked, streaming_hold=false, retry_policy=auto (1 retry)

Jin: So retries could be compounding. If the client sees a truncated args JSON in chunk 2, it might trigger a local repair attempt and resend, while server later emits the completed func_call chunk, causing duplicate execution.

Alex: exactly. What's worse: our tool-level idempotency isn't wired for this (annotate creates side-effectful tasks). We got duplicate annotations in QA dataset.

Maria: We should add a deterministic call-id embedded in args and have tool ignore duplicates for canary. Short-term mitigations:
- force streaming_hold=true for int8 canaries
- increase client-side chunk reassembly tolerance
- add call-id to func args

Sasha: Also want an eval: run n=500 canned prompts comparing fp16 vs int8 streaming chunks and measure funccall_dup_rate + parse_fail_rate.

Jin: I'll run a small experiment. Quick script:
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 500); do
  curl -s -X POST $API -d '{"model":"harbor-lite-int8","stream":true,"prompt":"@SAMPLE"}' > out/$i.txt
  # parse out function call occurrences
done
# compute dup rate
```

Jin: preliminary 100-run: int8 dup_rate=3.0% parse_fail=1.2%  fp16 dup_rate=0.0% parse_fail=0.1%

Alex: ok that's actionable. Can we pause int8 streaming canaries and keep batch/serve mode for now?

canary-bot: Pausing streaming canaries for model harbor-lite-int8. Notified owners: @Alex, @Jin

Sasha: Also add a lint in the streaming client: if a func_call chunk contains unclosed JSON (ends with comma or missing brace) don't immediately call the tool; buffer up to 250ms or until complete chunk received.

Maria: +1. Add telemetry flags: emit chunk_boundary_token for every streaming emit so we can correlate quant flushes -> boundary.

Jin: I'll instrument and run the 500-run bench. Will attach csv when done.

Alex: thanks. Action items:
- Jin: run and attach bench + raw chunks (due EOD)\n- Maria: implement call-id wrapper for annotate in canary tool shim (tomorrow)
- Sasha: add client-side buffer heuristic + small fuzz harness (tomorrow)
- Ops: keep streaming canaries paused for harbor-lite-int8 until we get <0.5% dup_rate

StructBot: Note: created ticket INF-9483 "streaming chunk boundary duplication - int8 canary" assigned to Jin/Maria/Sasha

Alex: Filing follow-up doc about long-term: kernel-level emission determinism and runtime sequence alignment to avoid func_call split across emit boundaries. Will ping infra.
